title: OpStream: templated admin flows and conditional escalation tasks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build OpStream: a lightweight admin utility that exposes curated incident/playbook flows as first-class tasks. Each flow is a sequence of discrete task steps (checks, remediation commands, rollbacks, communications) with conditional branching and built-in telemetry hooks. The goal is to reduce time-to-diagnosis for oncall, standardize triage steps, and enable safe automation for common support patterns without requiring full runbook orchestration platform adoption.
background_and_rationale: Current runbook-as-code work is powerful but heavyweight for routine ops: engineers often open ad-hoc tickets for common support work (KV cache clears, model fallback toggles, routing policy changes). OpStream targets those frequent scenarios by providing templates + an operator CLI and Slack actions that execute guarded task sequences. This reduces manual errors, provides audit logs, and keeps SLOs visible during interventions.
design_decisions: Represent each step as an idempotent primitive (check, exec, notify, wait, rollback) so templates compose safely
Use a simple state machine persisted in OpsDB instead of heavy workflow engines for lowest ops friction
Guard destructive steps behind explicit approval gates; support single-step rollback templates by default
Instrument every step with trace_id and token_cost metadata to feed Console observability dashboards
implementation_plan: Phase 1: implement primitives and a JSON/YAML template schema + CLI (opstreamctl)
Phase 2: Slack slash-commands and interactive messages for triggering templates with variables
Phase 3: Add conditional branching and timeouts, expose telemetry to Console via /internal/opstream endpoint
Phase 4: Canary templates with two product teams, gather metrics, iterate on guard UX
acceptance_criteria: opstreamctl can list, validate, and run templates in dev environment
Triggered flows run to completion with step-by-step logs persisted to OpsDB
Slack action triggers a template that requires one approver before destructive steps
Console dashboard shows per-template execution latency and failure rate
Two production-like templates are approved by SRE and used in canary by two teams
technical_notes: Prototype will use a small Go service that reads templates from a canonical repository (s3 / GCS). Persistence will be a new OpsDB table with soft-delete and an events stream for Console. Avoid introducing new long-lived scheduler processes; use ephemeral workers invoked by the service to run step primitives. We'll reuse existing KMS integration for sealing approval tokens.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive actions. Mitigation: default approval gates + dry-run mode + audit trail
Risk: template drift and stale steps. Mitigation: template schema validation and CI linting for references to runtime-only operations
Risk: noisy notifications. Mitigation: rate limit Slack messages and batch summary notifications
progress_updates: 2025-03-01: Ticket created and scoped during infra sync. Initial proto idea from SRE rotation notes.
2025-03-04: Spike completed — basic opstreamctl can validate a local template and emit an execution plan (poC repo: github.com/redwood/opstream-proto, PR #12)
2025-03-06: Architecture review with Platform team. Agreed to use OpsDB events stream and existing KMS. Action item: add approval token API.
2025-03-08: Security reviewed schema for secrets handling; approved conditioned on ephemeral KMS-wrapped tokens and no plaintext storage.
2025-03-10: First Slack prototype messages working in #ops-test. Need UX polish for approval modal and variable prompts. PR for opstreamctl CLI: https://github.com/redwood/opstream/pull/34
open_questions: Should OpStream templates be editable in Console UI or only via code repo?
What RBAC model maps to template approval gates (team-level vs role-level)?
How do we present per-step token_cost to non-engineering oncall users in Slack?
next_steps: Deliver minimal opstreamctl with 'list/validate/run/dry-run' commands (owner: Ethan)
Build Slack interactive approval flow and add feature flag for canary teams (owner: Maya Singh)
Create two starter templates: 'cache-clear-safe' and 'model-fallback-to-quantized' and onboard canary teams
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on schema safety (no plaintext secrets), approval UX, and telemetry hooks. If you see a template that would run admin console DB migrations, flag it — migrations must remain manual.
qa_plan: Unit tests for template validation, integration tests using a sandbox environment that records OpsDB events, and an automated dry-run test for all starter templates in CI. Manual run through with SREs during canary week.
follow_ups: Post-canary: add rollback-by-tag feature and automate runbook-to-template imports
Explore audit-log export to SIEM for enterprise customers
